method: Second rare-cultivar pass spanning France, Greece and Kyrgyzstan. Identity, pedigree and area/phenology facts retain their source context. Historical area or trial observations are not treated as current commercial acreage.

profiles.name: Romorantin

historicalStatus.legalAnchor: Cour-Cheverny PDO uses Romorantin B as its sole principal wine grape variety in the cited product-specification publication

identity.geneticParentage: Pinot × Gouais Blanc family cross reported by French technical sources
identity.conservatory: approximately 50 clones planted in Loir-et-Cher in 2007

viticulture.pruning: can be pruned long or short
viticulture.site: French technical record recommends adapted, early terroirs

researchNotes: Historical area series is explicitly time-stamped; 79 ha is the 2018 French figure in the current Plantgrape record, not a 2026 acreage claim.
Sensory claims from generic secondary sources are not promoted into the structural matrix without separate evidence.

profiles.name: Limniona

historicalStatus.recovery: national wine-body source states the quality potential was identified when only a few vines remained, followed by research and microvinification
historicalStatus.currentDistribution: now cultivated in multiple Greek areas, with some plantings still experimental according to Wines of Greece

identity.helleniferaSelectionProgram: more than 10 old vineyards visited; 13 Limniona clones selected; experimental field established

diseaseAndClimate.drought: Hellenifera reports drought resistance in its clonal/agronomic profile

viticulture.cluster: medium-sized grapes with large berries in Hellenifera profile

researchNotes: Limniona must never normalize to Limnio; UC Davis FPS explicitly treats them as separate Greek varieties.
Wines of Greece sensory and ageing descriptions are source observations, not universal numeric tasting-matrix values.

Current Kyrgyz planting status requires new primary or institutional evidence before generation-safe use.

queuePolicy: Queue membership does not establish synonymy, genetics, current commercial planting, legal wine use, or generation safety.
